decisions.statement: The feed sends a list of stoplights and only the first is drawn.
A stoplight carrying an empty figure draws no signal rather than a black ring.
A cost the feed carries is drawn whatever color that cost reached.
A cost carrying the surplus that cost was colored with counts down to that surplus.
The wait is aimed from the figure as of the moment drawn rather than as taken.
A rung already crossed is never aimed at.
The rung under a crossed rung is aimed at.
The wait shrinks a second a second whatever the rate.
The rate fixes the moment only.
A cost carrying no such surplus keeps the caption the readout's page names.
The color is read again from the surplus as of the moment drawn.
The surplus the color is read again from is the figure in hours rather than a tier.
A cost drawn yellow is yellow while the surplus is over minus four hours.
A cost drawn yellow is red while the surplus is over minus eight hours.
A cost drawn red is red while the surplus is over minus eight hours.
A cost drawn yellow or red is black once the surplus is minus eight hours.
A cost sent red is priced in one of two bands that fall together.
Which band a cost is priced in is read back off the color the server drew rather than the figure.
A figure is floored before that figure is sent.
A band read off a figure reads wrong.
A cost drawn any color but yellow or red is left as the server drew that cost.
A cost carrying a surplus that is not falling is left as the server drew it.
The moment the wait runs out is the moment the color moves and the aim changes.
That moment is handed to the feed.
The feed draws the tile again at that moment.
Nothing here says which rungs a scale has.

definition: the tile drawing what an hour of the block a person is in costs
